properties.name: Every project on the builder's box installs from the maintainer's LIVE WORKING TREE, because the kit path is a symlink to the development checkout
properties.statement: FLO2 F15 reported `reflow2 init .` refusing to install all 30 skills — "['audience','summary'] are not read by every harness" — and concluded that "the validator and the skill library disagree with each other". MEASURED 2026-09-19 and the conclusion does not hold for any committed state. ① `readlink -f ~/.local/share/reflow2/kit` resolves to `/home/ajs7/project/reflow2`: the kit path is a SYMLINK to the development checkout, made 2026-08-07, sharing its .git. ② `git log --all -S` for those top-level keys on a skill file finds them in NO commit: `summary`/`audience` have lived inside `metadata:` since they were introduced (bc157eb, PR #541), because the installer's harness-portability check refused the top-level form during that very PR and the fields were moved to satisfy it. ③ Running the installer today into a throwaway repo exits 0 and writes the full set. SO WHAT FLO2 MET WAS AN UNCOMMITTED WORKING TREE, mid-edit, half-way through the change that fixed it — not a released or committed state, and not a disagreement between the validator and the library. The validator was right and its input was a half-finished edit. ⭐ THE REAL FINDING IS LARGER THAN THE ONE REPORTED: a consumer project on this machine installs from whatever the maintainer's editor holds at that second. Every `init` in flo2, bhome or SeattleArch has been reading the dev tree, so a consumer's install can be broken, or silently ahead of every release, by an edit in progress. The workaround flo2 documented — skip `init`, since the machine-wide registration is enough — sidesteps it without addressing it.
